source_title: Cut down on digital distractions
passage_paraphrase: Suggests muting social app alerts during work hours while keeping call and text alerts on for emergencies, because even a silenced phone buzzes and pulls attention.
boundary_rule: alerts sorted by who needs to reach you
interpretation_note: Sorts notifications by urgency, so the phone is partly legitimate and only social alerts count as the distraction.

source_title: Cut down on digital distractions
passage_paraphrase: Recommends telling a friend or classmate your goals and studying together, even online, and says working with a tutor makes students less likely to check Instagram.
boundary_rule: presence of another person curbs checking
interpretation_note: Treats checking Instagram as a default temptation that other people help hold back.

source_title: Cut down on digital distractions
passage_paraphrase: Says quitting social media entirely is unrealistic because connection matters right now, and proposes scheduled 15-minute social media breaks plus browser extensions that limit time.
interpretation_note: Admits social media meets a social need, but the fix is still time-boxing.

institution: University of Missouri (Center for Academic Success & Excellence)
source_title: Director's Corner: Stay focused
passage_paraphrase: A center director lists eliminating distractions as a study tip and uses a recent outage of major apps to show how tethered students are to technology and how social media becomes a time waster.
imagined_audience: students heading into a long semester
interpretation_note: Uses an outage as evidence of dependence, which frames the problem as attachment more than specific uses.

source_title: 5 tips for a successful finals week
passage_paraphrase: Advises putting away or turning off the phone, TV and video games while studying.
interpretation_note: The phone is lumped with TV and games, so this is a device judgment more than a social media judgment.

source_title: 5 tips for a successful finals week
passage_paraphrase: Adds that students who need the phone for education apps should use Do Not Disturb to block text and social media notifications.
boundary_rule: phone is acceptable when used for coursework apps
interpretation_note: The same device is allowed when its purpose is educational, and notifications are the thing to silence.

source_title: Strategies for Success
passage_paraphrase: Says media multitasking such as texting or browsing social media while studying is especially harmful, citing unnamed studies linking it to lower test performance and GPAs.
interpretation_note: The authority comes from unnamed studies, which is a place to check the evidence trail.

source_title: Strategies for Success
passage_paraphrase: Offers to lend a Pomodoro timer at the service desk for students who find a phone or web browser distracting as a timer.
boundary_rule: phone timer is fine unless it distracts you
interpretation_note: The institution supplies a non-phone tool, which treats the phone as the hazard.

source_title: Focus While Studying
passage_paraphrase: Opens by asking whether the reader studies with the phone nearby and bounces between Instagram, TikTok, VSCO and texts, and reassures them they are not alone.
interpretation_note: Normalizes the behavior through a list of named apps, which ties distraction to specific platforms.

source_title: Focus While Studying
passage_paraphrase: Suggests alternating study blocks with social media check-ins so students can focus without giving up their social media interests, and cites a 2019 study on Internet and Facebook use and academic distraction.
interpretation_note: Allowed use is defined by timing, and the citation gives the claim a visible source.

source_title: BYUH ohana offer guidance to students to improve their studying and work ethic
passage_paraphrase: A graduate student says he struggles with time management and with social media and phone distractions, and learned he needed a distraction-free environment to succeed.
interpretation_note: Personal testimony presents the solution as controlling the environment.

source_title: Tips for staying productive while working from home
passage_paraphrase: A staff member from an academic success center advises putting the phone away during homework to avoid social media distractions, and avoiding work in bed or in front of a television.
interpretation_note: Frames the home as an environment to be designed against distraction.

source_title: Article on student study habits
passage_paraphrase: A student says social media usually distracts them while studying, so they leave the phone in their room and study in a common area.
interpretation_note: Self-management by physical separation.

source_title: Article on student study habits
passage_paraphrase: The same article notes that other students use their phones as tools to help them study.
boundary_rule: phone used as a study tool
interpretation_note: One line acknowledges a productive use but does not develop it.

source_title: Activities to do at WSU instead of doomscrolling
passage_paraphrase: Describes doomscrolling as a popular way for students to procrastinate and suggests studying with a friend or in a group.
interpretation_note: Distraction is described as procrastination, and the remedy is social.

source_title: Activities to do at WSU instead of doomscrolling
passage_paraphrase: A peer academic coach says students often name their phone and doomscrolling as a major roadblock, and recommends 25-minute study blocks with distractions put away followed by short breaks.
boundary_rule: study blocks with the phone away
interpretation_note: Peer coach voice, with a time-boxing technique as the fix.

source_title: Activities to do at WSU instead of doomscrolling
passage_paraphrase: Suggests booking appointments with advisors, peer coaches, tutors or counseling as a way to refocus on goals instead of scrolling.
interpretation_note: Responsibility shifts toward campus services.

source_title: Increase productivity with these 10 student success tips
passage_paraphrase: An interviewee says social media in general probably disrupts studying, but technology also offers benefits that can help with studying.
boundary_rule: depends on whether the technology is used to study
interpretation_note: Splits social media from technology, then keeps both possibilities open.

source_title: Increase productivity with these 10 student success tips
passage_paraphrase: Says social media has been linked to harm to mental health and sleep through its addictiveness, which can then disrupt studying.
interpretation_note: Distraction is explained as a downstream effect of wellbeing problems.

source_title: Increase productivity with these 10 student success tips
passage_paraphrase: Quotes an interviewee who believes procrastinating on social media can happen to anyone and should not make students feel ashamed.
interpretation_note: A rare non-moralizing framing of distraction.

source_title: Start the semester Warrior strong
passage_paraphrase: Advises setting the phone to Do Not Disturb during study sessions and lists Netflix and social media among distractions that can derail study goals in virtual learning.
interpretation_note: Social media sits in a list with streaming and chores, so the category is 'things competing for attention'.

source_title: Paying Attention to Distraction (workshop slides)
passage_paraphrase: A workshop slide lists phones, notifications, social media and games as digital distractions for students to identify.
interpretation_note: Social media appears as one list entry with no distinction between uses.

source_title: Article on studying and social media
passage_paraphrase: A student says they study in a lounge without a phone or computer when they need serious work, calling them a distraction, but adds that Facebook breaks can make studying feel lighter.
boundary_rule: breaks are fine, focused work is not
interpretation_note: The same platform is a distraction during work and a relief during a break.

source_title: Opinion | Too much social media could affect grades
passage_paraphrase: A columnist argues that earlier generations of students managed without social media and current students can too.
interpretation_note: Uses past students as precedent, which assumes college life has stayed comparable.

source_title: Opinion | Too much social media could affect grades
passage_paraphrase: Advises putting the phone away during long study or writing sessions and claims even texting can pull students away from their degree.
interpretation_note: Extends the problem from social media to any phone communication.

source_title: Opinion | Too much social media could affect grades
passage_paraphrase: Concedes students can use social media to stay socially updated but asks them to limit it during the crunch period before finals.
interpretation_note: The boundary moves with the academic calendar.

source_title: Study efficiently with a timer
passage_paraphrase: Says research indicates some activities during study breaks can boost productivity, while social media may have the opposite effect.
boundary_rule: what you do on a break matters
interpretation_note: Social media is singled out among break activities.

source_title: Beware of the dangers of doomscrolling
passage_paraphrase: A counseling services director says excessive social media use affects mental health, self-esteem, sleep and academic performance.
interpretation_note: Harm is tied to quantity, not to use itself.

source_title: Beware of the dangers of doomscrolling
passage_paraphrase: Notes that school, work and social lives make it unrealistic for students to leave screens entirely, so they should aim to reduce time on phones and social media.
interpretation_note: Accepts that social media is woven into student life.

source_title: Beware of the dangers of doomscrolling
passage_paraphrase: The director suggests making social apps harder to reach, such as burying them in folders, so students pause to think about why they are going online; the article also names apps that set daily time limits.
interpretation_note: Adds friction as a design tactic and ties good use to having a reason.

source_title: College students struggle to balance social media and mental health
passage_paraphrase: A counseling intern says social media is a big distractor and that students scroll to avoid starting assignments or facing difficult situations.
interpretation_note: Distraction is read as avoidance.

source_title: College students struggle to balance social media and mental health
passage_paraphrase: The intern attributes part of the difficulty of stopping to platform design, describing algorithms that keep showing similar content.
interpretation_note: A rare example that locates responsibility outside the individual.

source_title: College students struggle to balance social media and mental health
passage_paraphrase: The intern also says starting the day with short videos can make it harder to shift into productive tasks later.
interpretation_note: Frames the timing of use as the problem.

source_title: Doom Scrolling and Downtime: Finding Time to Breathe
passage_paraphrase: Says giving up social media entirely is unrealistic and recommends using it purposefully rather than to fill free time.
interpretation_note: Defines good use by intention, which is close to the purpose-based distinction this project cares about.

source_title: Doom Scrolling and Downtime: Finding Time to Breathe
passage_paraphrase: Recommends pausing before opening an app, using phone screen-time limits, and filtering the content in feeds.
interpretation_note: Pairs a mindfulness habit with built-in phone tools.

source_title: Binghamton University students say doom scrolling is hurting their mental health and focus
passage_paraphrase: Students report stepping back from their accounts because negative content affects mood, sleep and focus, and one says having a phone nearby makes it hard to stay on task.
interpretation_note: Distraction and mood are described together.

source_title: Binghamton University students say doom scrolling is hurting their mental health and focus
passage_paraphrase: A quoted expert describes social media as an avoidance technique linked to stress and recommends deleting apps, setting limits or choosing other free-time activities.
interpretation_note: Distraction is explained as a response to stress.

source_title: Post-Election Blues? Here Are Some Tips
passage_paraphrase: Student-written wellbeing tips after an election advise not to doom-scroll and to set app time limits in phone settings.
interpretation_note: Here the problem is news content and emotional load, not study time.

source_title: Adams Center blog post on a LinkedIn session
passage_paraphrase: Describes career center staff teaching students to use LinkedIn for networking, citing that most recruiters use it and most jobs come from referrals, and helping students build profiles and find alumni connections.
interpretation_note: Professional use is presented as plainly productive, backed by unsourced statistics.

source_title: News release on LinkedIn for Job Seekers workshops
passage_paraphrase: Cites a CareerBuilder survey saying employers who screen candidates online look for qualifications and a professional presence, and promotes LinkedIn workshops for job seekers.
interpretation_note: Social media presence is something employers evaluate, so it is both opportunity and scrutiny.

source_title: Career Center post on using social media in the job search
passage_paraphrase: Acknowledges the familiar warnings about social media and job hunting but argues it can be extremely helpful, calling LinkedIn the most underrated site for networking.
interpretation_note: Explicitly reverses the danger story.

source_title: Career Center post on using social media in the job search
passage_paraphrase: Says many students do not have a LinkedIn account and points them to a career center guide and an alumni-led workshop.
interpretation_note: Not having an account is framed as the gap.

source_title: Three Unique Ways to Use Social Media in College
passage_paraphrase: Recommends following campus offices and organizations on social media to learn about services and opportunities.
interpretation_note: Social media is treated as an information channel for campus.

source_title: Three Unique Ways to Use Social Media in College
passage_paraphrase: Notes that some companies and organizations use their social accounts to advertise jobs.
interpretation_note: Feeds become a job board.

source_title: Lehigh Career Center gives advice on LinkedIn networking
passage_paraphrase: Career staff describe LinkedIn as a social network for business, useful for following companies and connecting with people in an organization, and note tens of thousands of students and alumni are connected.
interpretation_note: Institutional scale is used as proof of value.

source_title: LinkedIn Workshop For Students: March 3
passage_paraphrase: Career staff contrast Facebook, described mainly as a place to socialize, with LinkedIn, described as a site for professional purposes.
interpretation_note: The boundary is drawn by platform, not by what a person actually does there.

source_title: LinkedIn Workshop For Students: March 3
passage_paraphrase: Says networking is key to finding jobs and internships in a tough market, so students benefit from knowing the platform.
interpretation_note: Economic pressure is the reason given.

institution: University of Notre Dame / Saint Mary's College (The Observer)
source_title: Students network for job openings using LinkedIn
passage_paraphrase: Career staff say social networks are now part of the job search and help connect alumni and students, but warn students to behave professionally online.
interpretation_note: Benefit comes with a conduct requirement.

source_title: Using LinkedIn to prepare for future employment
passage_paraphrase: A career services center encourages LinkedIn use for networking and says nearly all recruiters use it, a figure given without a source.
interpretation_note: A precise-sounding number does the persuading.

source_title: 10 ways students can build a professional LinkedIn profile
passage_paraphrase: Says LinkedIn is not a place for memes or daily meals and advises professional posts and a header image showing professional life instead of friends and fun.
interpretation_note: Norms define acceptable content within a platform.

source_title: 10 ways students can build a professional LinkedIn profile
passage_paraphrase: Suggests starting by connecting with alumni, who were once in the student's position.
interpretation_note: Belonging to the school is used as a networking asset.

source_title: Job networking websites help students kickstart careers
passage_paraphrase: A career center associate director calls LinkedIn a powerful networking tool, especially with less face-to-face contact, and the center reviews student profiles.
interpretation_note: Remote conditions raise the value of online networking.

source_title: Students get LinkedIn to professional world
passage_paraphrase: Says preparing for a job search now involves social media, and experts consider a LinkedIn profile essential.
interpretation_note: Moves from optional to required.

source_title: Using LinkedIn to get Ahead (event listing)
passage_paraphrase: A workshop listing says LinkedIn can help students explore careers, see how majors translate to jobs, find alumni and connect with people they know.
interpretation_note: Frames the platform as career exploration, not only job hunting.

source_title: Article on making friends through social media
passage_paraphrase: A student introduced herself on an Instagram page for incoming freshmen, which grew into a WhatsApp group chat of nearly 200 people and led to friendships.
interpretation_note: Belonging is built through a platform, not despite it.

source_title: Article on making friends through social media
passage_paraphrase: Cites a researcher saying college friendships can have academic as well as social benefits, and describes a group chat that began in a breakout room and led to studying together.
interpretation_note: Connects social ties to academic benefit, which complicates the study versus social split.

source_title: Incoming students build community online
passage_paraphrase: Reports that incoming students use social media pages, group chats and Discord servers to meet before arriving, and that clubs watch these pages to recruit.
interpretation_note: Both students and organizations use the platforms deliberately.

source_title: Incoming students build community online
passage_paraphrase: A club member says a group chat made it easier to make plans, while another student says they skip group chats and prefer talking to people in person.
interpretation_note: Includes a dissenting voice, which is unusual in advice writing.

source_title: Jumpstart your college experience with social media
passage_paraphrase: The student author describes social media as a stepping stone that helped overcome social anxiety, find a roommate and join clubs.
interpretation_note: A student voice on an official site presents social media as a tool for adjustment.

source_title: Online introductions ease first-year transition
passage_paraphrase: Students say a Facebook group let them hear about clubs before move-in, and commuters value specialized group chats for forming friendships before arriving.
interpretation_note: Commuter students are named as a group with distinct needs.

source_title: How to Be Involved in University Communities as an Online Student
passage_paraphrase: A guide for online students recommends following school social accounts, joining student-run pages and starting a class chat group, and links community to staying focused and supported.
interpretation_note: Ties community directly to focus, the opposite of the distraction story.

source_title: Social media enhances your online student experience
passage_paraphrase: A blog for online students recommends following the school's social pages for news and study tips and posting questions to fellow students.
interpretation_note: Social media is a source of study help.

source_title: Introducing Facebook Campus
passage_paraphrase: A platform announcement presents a campus-only space where classmates can find clubs, study groups and dorm chat rooms, framed around staying connected during remote learning.
interpretation_note: The platform defines productive use as campus connection.

source_title: TikTok adds Campus Hub feature for US college students
passage_paraphrase: Trade press describes a feature letting verified students from thousands of US universities join group chats of up to 300 classmates, and notes that similar campus groups have attracted outsiders targeting students.
interpretation_note: Benefit and risk are presented together.
